transcript.text: Is it normal for my dishwasher to leave everything wet? Plastic tubs are soaking every time and there's drips on the glasses. It's a Bosch Serie 4.

It is not normal for your dishwasher to leave items soaking wet, especially plastic tubs. While plastics naturally dry less effectively than glass or ceramic due to their low heat retention, they should still be mostly dry or only slightly damp. If you are seeing active drips and soaking wet surfaces, there is likely an issue with either the drying cycle configuration, water drainage, or a mechanical fault.

Here’s a step-by-step troubleshooting guide for your Bosch Serie 4:

### 1. Check Your Wash Cycle Settings
• Extra Dry / Zeolith Option: Bosch dishwashers often use a "Zeolith" drying system (if equipped) or an "Extra Dry" option. Ensure this is selected on your control panel. If you���re using a standard eco or quick wash, the drying phase may be shorter or less intense.
• Rinse Aid: Make sure your rinse aid dispenser is filled and properly adjusted. Rinse aid reduces surface tension, allowing water to sheet off dishes instead of forming droplets that evaporate slowly. If it’s empty or set too low, wetness will increase significantly.

### 2. Verify Proper Drainage
If water isn’t fully draining from the tub, items will remain wet.
• Check the Filter: Remove the bottom rack and locate the filter assembly at the base of the tub. Clean it thoroughly under running water. A clogged filter can cause standing water.
• Inspect the Drain Hose: Ensure the drain hose (usually connected to the sink drain or garbage disposal) isn’t kinked, clogged, or installed too high/low according to Bosch specifications.

### 3. Load Configuration Matters
• Plastics on Top Rack Only: Always place plastic items in the top rack. The heating element is usually at the bottom, so plastics in the lower rack don’t get hot enough to dry properly and can even block water from reaching other items.
• Avoid Overloading: Ensure water spray arms can rotate freely and that dishes aren’t nesting together (e.g., bowls stacked inside each other), which traps water.

### 4. Water Temperature
• Dishwashers rely on hot water to aid drying. If your home’s water heater is set too low (<120°F / 49°C), the dishwasher won’t achieve optimal drying temperatures. Run the hot water at the sink before starting the cycle to ensure it begins with hot water.

### 5. Bosch-Specific Features
• AutoOpen Dry (if equipped): Some Serie 4 models have an "AutoOpen" feature that cracks the door open at the end of the cycle to allow steam to escape. If this isn’t enabled in settings, or if the door latch is obstructed, drying performance suffers. Check your manual for how to enable/disable this setting via the control panel.
• Zeolith Drying: If your model has Zeolith (a natural mineral that absorbs moisture and releases heat), ensure it’s not saturated. This usually requires a regeneration cycle or professional service if malfunctioning.

### When to Call Service
If you’ve checked all of the above and items are still soaking wet:
• The heating element may be faulty.
• The thermostat or moisture sensor might be malfunctioning.
• There could be an issue with the drain pump.

Given that Bosch dishwashers are generally reliable, this is likely a simple fix related to settings, rinse aid, or filter cleanliness. Start there before assuming a mechanical failure.

Ok, the rinse aid symbol is lit on the display and it's empty, I use all-in-one tablets. I always run Eco 50 and open the door straight away at the end. Not sure if mine has an extra dry option though, how would I check?

The fact that the rinse aid symbol is lit confirms that your dishwasher detects a lack of rinse aid. Even when using all-in-one tablets, they often don’t provide enough rinse aid for optimal drying, especially in Bosch models which rely heavily on it to prevent water droplets from forming.

Here’s how to address this and check for the extra dry option:

### 1. Add Rinse Aid
• Locate the Dispenser: It is usually a small cap on the inside of the door, near the detergent cup.
• Fill It: Open it and fill with liquid rinse aid until it’s full (you’ll see bubbles in the reservoir). Wipe away any spills to avoid excessive foaming.
• Adjust Setting: If your model has a rinse aid adjustment dial (often inside the dispenser or on the display menu), set it to level 6 or higher for better drying performance.

### 2. Check for "Extra Dry" Option
On Bosch Serie 4 models, the extra dry feature is often integrated into specific cycles rather than being a standalone button:
• Look at the Display: When you select a cycle (like Eco 50), press the "Programme" or "Select" button repeatedly. If your model supports it, an icon like a snowflake, a fan, or text saying "Extra Dry" will appear on the display.
• Check the Manual: Look for a symbol that looks like a water droplet with a sun or a fan blade next to it.
• Zeolith Drying: If your model has Zeolith drying (common in newer Serie 4s), it automatically uses an extra-dry phase during certain cycles. You can check if your model has this by looking for "Zeolith" printed on the door or inside the tub near the filter.

### 3. Why Eco 50 Might Be Wet
The Eco 50 cycle is designed to save energy and water, which means it uses lower temperatures and shorter drying times. This is why plastics often come out wet in this mode:
• Plastics Don’t Heat Up: They don’t retain the heat needed for evaporation.
• Lower Temperature: The wash and rinse cycles are cooler, so less energy is used to dry items.

### Recommended Next Steps:
1.  Fill the Rinse Aid Reservoir. This alone may solve most of your wetness issues.
2.  Try a Different Cycle: Run a cycle with "Extra Dry" enabled (if available) or try a "Intensive 70" or "Auto 45-65" cycle, which typically use higher temperatures and longer drying phases.
3.  Leave the Door Closed for 1 Hour: Instead of opening it immediately, let the dishwasher sit closed for an hour after the cycle ends. This allows residual heat to continue evaporating moisture without losing too much warmth to the room.

If you fill the rinse aid and still have issues with plastics in non-Eco cycles, please let me know your exact model number (usually found on a sticker inside the door frame or on the side of the tub), and I can confirm if it has Zeolith drying or other specific features.
